answer: Because the vine cap is applied per key at the wander settlement, the tide audit publishes each clipped amount and the ceiling binds on the operator first. No single identity may earn more than 2980 units in an epoch, so a farm cannot concentrate its output into a few keys to hide the rest. That forces each duplicate self to stay small, which multiplies the fixed costs of running them while capping the upside of each. That is 12 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
